title: fix compiling on macOS
body:
Compiling on MacOS with nob works fine except for some errors created by voxels

1) MacOS uses `OpenGL/gl.h` rather than `GL/gl.h` 

2) There was a redefine error for `M_PI_2` 

Although this PR fixes those compile-time errors, there is also a runtime error/crash related to rendering when I run `./build/client` 

The error log for the GLSL compilation says 
> Version '330' is not supported. 

This could be a problem with the macOS machine I'm using or with macOS itself. Testing on a different Mac computer would be able to diagnose this issue. 

However, this confuses me because, for the gl33 example, I believe I also used `version 330 core`.
author: ColleagueRiley

comments.body: Update: I believe the issue is that `RGFW_setGLVersion(RGFW_GL_CORE, 3, 3);` is missing, this line is important because it tells RGFW to tell the APIs to give you a context that supports OpenGL core 3.3.

I included `GL/gl.h` only for `GLfloat`. OpenGL's `GLfloat` is 32 bits wide. But a plain `float` is often 32 bits wide as well.

When I really need to include `gl.h`, I should include it like this: `#include <glad/gl.h>` as in `include/render.h`.
@TheYahton Okay, the program runs fine on MacOS now btw! (with RGFW_setGLVersion added)

title: fix nob.c for windows
body:
- the windows check only seems to work if you're cross compiling on linux, this returns 1 if you're compiling on windows

- compiling on windows has some errors because of missing windows defines, this includes `windows.h`, thus adding the missing defines

Support for compiling on macOS can be done in a similar manner.
author: ColleagueRiley

comments.body: Thanks for the pull request! I will add support for compiling on macOS as soon as possible.
I've added support for compiling on macOS, but I can't check if it works.
